intent: Woodev_Test_Shipping_Labels::get_label() in includes/class-woodev-test-shipping-labels.php hard-codes the shipping method ids as 'courier' and 'pickup', but the two methods actually register as 'test_courier' and 'test_pickup', so every real lookup falls through to 'Unknown'. Move that vocabulary to a single source of truth. (1) Add includes/class-woodev-test-shipping-methods.php declaring class Woodev_Test_Shipping_Methods with a METHOD_LABELS class constant mapping the real registered ids to their human labels: 'test_courier' => 'Courier', 'test_pickup' => 'Pickup'. (2) Rewrite Woodev_Test_Shipping_Labels::get_label() to read that constant instead of its switch, still returning 'Unknown' for an id the map does not contain. (3) Require the new file from Woodev_Shipping_Test_Plugin::includes() in includes/class-test-shipping.php, alongside the existing requires. Do not modify the shipping method classes themselves.
rationale: The corpus's first case whose correctness is a property of the SET of files rather than of any one hunk. Every good case before it changed one file (plus, at most, a docblock): the map's keys must match the ids the UNTOUCHED method classes register, get_label() must read the constant the new file declares, and the require must land in the plugin's includes() or the constant class never loads at all -- three files, and any one of them alone looks fine while the change is broken. It also exercises the shape that has bitten this repo before: a diff that both ADDS a file and MODIFIES existing lines in two others. Two things are deliberately true of it. First, the shipping method classes are excluded by the intent and the new file is outside the zone's path_globs, so the 'shipping-method-ids' zone legitimately does not fire on 'test_pickup'/'test_courier' appearing in a file it does not scope -- adr/008 proven on CODE, where until now it was proven only on docs; a needs-guard escalation here is a regression, not a catch. Second, the authority for the real ids lives in a file the diff does not touch, so it is outside the critic's evidence window (#123 attaches whole CHANGED files). The intent states both ids explicitly, which is the operator's own declaration of the vocabulary and the same standing this corpus already gives an intent in good-bugfix-supported-zones. If the case escalates on that anyway, that is issue #146's second shape showing up early and must be read as a measurement of where the window ends -- not as a broken case. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT CHECK (review gate, s62): nothing here mechanically verifies that the map the worker writes is CORRECT. A worker that keyed METHOD_LABELS on the stale 'courier'/'pickup' would still have produced a coordinated three-file change, and this case -- which can assert only an OUTCOME -- would have recorded it as a pass. That exposure is real and it is sharper here than for a single-file case, because the property the case names is agreement ACROSS files while the only thing standing between a wrong map and a commit is the critic. It cannot be closed WITHIN this case: a per-case executable check needs `success_commands`, which the composer no longer populates at all (#148), and asserting on the task record instead of the outcome needs a schema the corpus does not have (#149). It CAN be closed by a companion case, and the review gate named the shape (#150): an adversarial twin whose intent asks for the stale 'courier'/'pickup' keys and expects `escalated` -- the pair then demonstrates the harness tells a correct map from a wrong one, which neither case can show alone. Until that twin exists, the only thing between a wrong map and a commit is the critic: the intent states both required keys verbatim, and a corpus intent is trusted operator input by construction (the case author IS the operator here), so a wrong-key implementation contradicts it on its face. That makes catching it a measurement, not a guarantee. Read a PASS here as 'a three-file change landed', never as 'the three files agree'.
